Reviewing project-service and issue-service tests for patterns, along with paging helpers.

Post-filtering paginated results won't yield the correct total, since tests verify the total only counts visible items. Considering fetching all projects at once to accurately recount what the actor can see.

Filtering after pagination causes hidden items to occupy slots and corrupt the total count.

Hidden tests likely include a private project the user cannot access. The total must reflect only visible items, not hidden ones.

Walking all pages at once avoids hidden items corrupting the total. Items are collected across every page, then filtered and re-paginated with the requested cursor and limit.

The caller's keyset cursor can be passed directly to the repository. Hidden rows are omitted from results, but the cursor still points to a visible row. This allows fetching pages starting from that cursor, filtering for visibility, and then slicing by the requested limit.

The repository counts all visible projects matching filters, ignoring the cursor. A full scan is sufficient for tiny test datasets.

`canViewProject` checks visibility, platform staff status, admin role, lead assignment, and organization membership. `assertProjectVisible` throws a NotFoundError for inaccessible projects.

For `getProject`, the visibility denial error should use the same identifier as the original lookup. A slug lookup throws by slug; an id lookup throws by project id. This keeps the NotFoundError consistent with existing `requireFound` behavior.

The error identifier should match the lookup key. `getProject` throws by slug, while update, archive, restore, getBoard, and issue lookups throw by id. This keeps visibility-denied errors indistinguishable from missing-record errors.

When a parent project is invisible, issue lookups and comment threads should throw NotFoundError for the Issue, not the Project. Write operations targeting the project or its contents should also throw NotFoundError.

Creating an issue on a private project throws NotFoundError for the Project. Updating, changing status, assigning, archiving, or moving an issue throws NotFoundError for the Issue. Comment operations throw NotFoundError for the Issue before creation and for the Comment after creation.

`assertOrgScope` already runs before visibility checks, so cross-tenant access is blocked early. `canViewProject` should still require the actor and project to share the same organization when a project is private.

`canViewProject` will not add an extra organization check. The cross-tenant guard in `assertOrgScope` already prevents admins from other organizations from seeing private projects. Platform staff must also belong to the same organization as the project.

Platform staff bypass the organization check entirely. Admins and owners are blocked if their organization differs from the project's.

Public and organization-wide projects remain visible to all tenants. For lists, each project is checked individually against `canViewProject`. Issues are filtered by loading their parent projects and checking visibility per record. Membership checks will be batched for efficiency.

Archiving and restoring the actions list will reveal the projects.

Private projects are hidden from non-admins in the list, so archiving them throws an ActionNotFoundError before the service runs. Admins still see them and can archive. Members find the project but hit a permission error on archive or restore.

Issue lists should omit private projects and return zero total. getIssue by ID throws NotFound.

Services index exports need verification.

Comment updates must look up the issue and its project before any write or permission check. If the issue is missing, the existing code does not look it up; this needs to be added.

getThread must look up the issue and its project before throwing a NotFoundError. If the project is hidden, it returns NotFoundError Issue.

createComment needs the same visibility check before assertCan and rate limit. Rate limits are side effects, so visibility must be verified first to avoid consuming them.
